```sql
WITH filtered AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT pv.product_id,
         pv.id AS variant_id,
         ol.order_id,
         ol.quantity,
         ol.line_total_cents
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = o.id
    JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
   WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
     AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
     AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
     AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
per_order AS (
  SELECT product_id,
         order_id,
         sum(quantity)          AS quantity,
         sum(line_total_cents)  AS revenue_cents
    FROM filtered
   GROUP BY product_id, order_id
),
per_product AS (
  SELECT product_id,
         count(*)                       AS order_count,
         sum(quantity)::bigint          AS quantity,
         sum(revenue_cents)             AS revenue_cents
    FROM per_order
   GROUP BY product_id
),
variants AS (
  SELECT product_id,
         count(*) AS variant_count
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, variant_id FROM filtered) d
   GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       pp.order_count,
       pp.quantity,
       pp.revenue_cents,
       v.variant_count
  FROM per_product pp
  JOIN variants v   ON v.product_id = pp.product_id
  JOIN products p   ON p.id = pp.product_id
 ORDER BY pp.quantity DESC, pp.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De aggregatie gebeurt eerst per (product, order), waardoor `count(DISTINCT o.id)` vervangen wordt door een `count(*)` en de dure sort op (product, order) verdwijnt. Het aantal distinct varianten wordt apart berekend uit een kleine set, en `sum(quantity)` is met `::bigint` gecast zodat het type gelijk blijft aan het origineel. Let op: bij gelijke waarden voor quantity en revenue blijft de volgorde niet-deterministisch, net als in het origineel; de winst is niet gemeten en moet met EXPLAIN ANALYZE gecontroleerd worden.
